title: FinitePushforwardPullbackComparison
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $(X,F)$ a torsion curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], $Y$ a curve over $k$, and $f:X\to Y$ finite over $k$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $A_X,A_Y$ be the underlying abelian sheaves after converting $F,f_*F$ to $\operatorname{ULift}\mathbb Z$-modules. In any cartesian square with upper arrow $b:X\prime\to X$, lower arrow $a:Y\prime\to Y$ and vertical arrows $f\prime,f$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], for every $q\ge0$ the pullback on $H^q(Y,A_Y)$ along $a$ is bijective (respectively surjective) if and only if the pullback on $H^q(X,A_X)$ along $b$ is bijective (respectively surjective) [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Section 03SB, Lemma 0A5D (lemma-finite-pushforward-statements); its proof uses Proposition 03QP (vanishing of R^qf_* for finite f), the Leray spectral sequence (Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 0733 sites-cohomology-lemma-apply-Leray) and Lemma 0959 (finite pushforward commutes with base change)

proof.text: Finite exchange is invertible. Apply bijective_edgeMap_baseChange for the two vertical comparison bijections and cohomology_edgeMap_baseChange for the commuting square.

proof.text: For bijections l and r satisfying v ∘ l = r ∘ w, bijectivity of w is equivalent to that of v. Surjectivity is equivalent too: lift through l in one direction and cancel the injective r in the other.

proof.text: The equivalence counit identifies the converted underlying abelian sheaves with the originals. Naturality of cohomology pullback gives commuting squares whose other maps are the cohomology bijections of these isomorphisms; apply the same elementary argument.
